title: Solve problems involving sequences and series in real and simulated situations

lessons.title: Arithmetic sequences and series
lessons.html:
Sequences with a constant difference

A sequence is an ordered list of numbers (terms). A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence. Sequences describe many farm situations: rows of trees, monthly loan repayments, herd growth, or a feeding programme that increases each week.

Arithmetic sequences

In an arithmetic sequence each term is found by adding the same number, the common difference d, to the previous term.

Example: a new feedlot ration starts at 2 kg per animal on day 1 and increases by 0,5 kg per day: 2; 2,5; 3; 3,5; ...

General term: Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term.

On day 10: T₁₀ = 2 + 9 × 0,5 = 6,5 kg.

Arithmetic series

The sum of the first n terms is:

Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] or Sₙ = n/2 (a + l) where l is the last term.

Total feed per animal over 10 days: S₁₀ = 10/2 × (2 + 6,5) = 5 × 8,5 = 42,5 kg. For 500 animals, that is 21 250 kg, or about 21,3 tonnes, of ration needed for the adaptation period.

Example: planting rows

A triangular block has 40 trees in the first row, and each row has 2 fewer trees than the one before. How many trees in 15 rows? a = 40, d = −2, n = 15. S₁₅ = 15/2 [80 + 14 × (−2)] = 7,5 × 52 = 390 trees.

Finding n

How many rows until a row has only 10 trees? 10 = 40 + (n − 1)(−2), so n − 1 = 15 and n = 16.

Sigma notation

A series can be written with Σ (sigma). For example Σ (from k = 1 to 5) of (3k + 1) = 4 + 7 + 10 + 13 + 16 = 50.

lessons.title: Geometric sequences, series and financial applications
lessons.html:
Sequences with a constant ratio

In a geometric sequence, each term is found by multiplying the previous term by the same number, the common ratio r.

General term: Tₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹

Example: a goat herd of 50 grows by 20% per year with no sales: 50; 60; 72; 86,4; ... Here r = 1,2. After 5 years (term 6): T₆ = 50 × 1,2⁵ ≈ 124 goats. Such growth is only possible if grazing and management allow it; real herds are limited by carrying capacity.

Geometric series

The sum of the first n terms:

Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) for r ≠ 1.

Example: a farm saves R10 000 in month 1 and increases savings by 5% each month. Total saved after 12 months: S₁₂ = 10 000 (1,05¹² − 1)/(0,05) ≈ 10 000 × 15,917 ≈ R159 171.

Infinite geometric series

If −1 < r < 1, the terms shrink and the sum approaches a limit: S∞ = a/(1 − r).

Example: a chemical residue halves each week after application, starting from 8 units: 8 + 4 + 2 + ... The total sum approaches 8/(1 − 0,5) = 16 units.

Financial applications

Compound interest is a geometric sequence: A = P(1 + i)ⁿ. Annuities, such as regular loan repayments or savings, are geometric series. For example, monthly deposits into a fund for a new tractor follow a geometric series where each deposit grows for a different number of periods.

Recognising the type

CheckArithmeticGeometric
PatternConstant differenceConstant ratio
GrowthLinearExponential
Term formulaa + (n − 1)da·rⁿ⁻¹

Key points

  • A sequence is a list of terms; a series is their sum.
  • Arithmetic: Tₙ = a + (n − 1)d and Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d].
  • Geometric: Tₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹ and Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1).
  • An infinite geometric series converges to a/(1 − r) when −1 < r < 1.
  • Compound interest and annuities are geometric applications.
